claim: Kim et al. found that unbiased Langevin simulations of their tetrahedrally lobed patchy particles started from a disordered gas gave spontaneous cubic diamond only for some parameter sets, nucleation and growth not being seen within reachable simulation times over much of the compression-ratio and size-ratio space, and mapped the stability region instead by melting runs started from the crystal.
validity_conditions: A MODEL RESULT. Tetrahedrally lobed patchy particles modelled as five spheres (four lobes and one central sphere for the patches) with an Alexander-de Gennes brush repulsion plus Asakura-Oosawa depletion (parameters in the SI, not in the file); Langevin dynamics in HOOMD-blue v2.9.7. Melting runs: 600 particles started in cubic diamond, 1e8 steps at time step 0.0001, stability judged by the fraction still diamond by common-neighbour analysis in OVITO; parameter sets outside the region melted completely. A melting run bounds where the crystal is stable, not where it can nucleate, so a plan reading this should not expect spontaneous diamond everywhere inside the region.
